page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-standard-48-lssd is an arm64-based server powered by 48 dedicated physical cores of the ARMv8 Neoverse-V2 architecture running at 3.0 GHz. It features 192 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per core. The server is equipped with 4020 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, offering high-speed local storage capacity without any integrated GPUs.

Performance benchmarks indicate exceptional multi-threaded capabilities and memory throughput. The server achieves top-tier results in Geekbench multi-core performance, software compilation with Clang, and PassMark database operations. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with read-only large block speeds reaching 286.75 GB/sec and write speeds at 143.04 GB/sec. Static web serving throughput is also in the top tier at 97.21 GB/sec, while Redis SET operations reach 98.12 million operations per second.

This hardware profile offers high qualitative cost efficiency for scale-out workloads due to its dedicated physical cores and dense local NVMe storage. The absence of hyperthreading ensures predictable execution times, though it may limit workloads that rely heavily on virtual thread overcommit. The server is highly suited for database hosting, software compilation pipelines, high-throughput static web serving, and multi-threaded data processing.

Lacking a GPU, this server excels in multi-threaded CPU and memory-bound tasks. Benchmarks show top-tier performance in software compilation, database operations, and static web serving, alongside strong memory bandwidth. The dedicated single-thread-per-core design provides highly predictable performance. This configuration is optimized for high-throughput databases, CI/CD compilation pipelines, Redis caching, and web serving workloads.
